target.title: fix(ai): fold case in OpenAI reasoning-effort matching (#102908)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeOpenAIReasoningEffort` (`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-reasoning-effort.ts`) passes effort names through unchanged, and `readCompatReasoningEfforts` keeps user-authored `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` entries as written. So a mixed-case requested effort (`"High"`) or a mixed-case compat entry (`"Low"`) fails the lowercase `.includes()` matching in `resolveOpenAIReasoningEffortForModel` / `supportsOpenAIReasoningEffort`. The miss doesn't fail loudly — it silently falls through the support ladder and returns a **different effort than the one the model actually supports** (e.g. requested `low` against a declared `["Low","MEDIUM","High"]` mis-ladders to another tier). Fixes #102908.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fold case on both sides of the boundary, using the normalization helpers this package already imports: `normalizeOpenAIReasoningEffort` now lowercases (efforts are matched against lowercase lists and sent to the API lowercase), and compat lists use the existing `normalizeStringEntriesLower` sibling helper. Disabled semantics (`"None"`/`"OFF"`) also work case-insensitively instead of falling through the ladder into an enabled effort. No new options or API surface; internal lowercase callers are byte-for-byte unaffected.

## User Impact

Operators writing `reasoningEffort`/`supportedReasoningEfforts` values in config with any casing get the effort they asked for, instead of a silently substituted tier (which changes model behavior and cost).

## Evidence

**Live OpenAI-compatible request run (wire capture, full recipe in PR comment):** real agent turn via `pnpm openclaw agent --local --thinking high` against a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint with user-authored mixed-case `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts: ["Low","MEDIUM","High"]`:

```
BEFORE (main):    POST /v1/chat/completions  → "reasoning_effort": "Low"    ← asked high, silently mis-laddered
AFTER  (this PR): POST /v1/chat/completions  → "reasoning_effort": "high"   ← correct tier and case
```

Two new regression tests **fail on current `main`** and pass with this PR:
```
main:    × matches mixed-case requested efforts     — expected 'low' to be 'high'   (mis-laddered)
         × folds case in compat-declared efforts    — ['Low','MEDIUM','High'] ≠ ['low','medium','high']
this PR: 12/12 pass
```
Consumer suites checked: `openai-responses-shared.test.ts` green; `stream-wrappers/openai.test.ts` has 2 pre-existing local failures (Codex attribution/user-agent, fail identically with main's reasoning-effort file — verified unrelated). `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.title: fix: ignore invalid Retry-After HTTP dates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where provider calls could treat malformed `Retry-After` HTTP-date headers as far-future retry windows when the date parser normalized invalid calendar dates such as `31 Feb`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guarded provider fetch path and the ChatGPT Responses retry path now parse RFC 1123, obsolete RFC 850, and asctime `Retry-After` HTTP dates by their components and verify the UTC date round trip before honoring the header. Numeric `Retry-After` values and valid obsolete RFC 850 dates keep their existing behavior, including the rolling 50-year two-digit-year window.

## User Impact

Malformed provider throttle headers no longer cause long retry sleeps or retry-bypass decisions. Valid HTTP-date `Retry-After` headers continue to work across the provider retry boundaries covered by this change.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: invalid calendar dates in `Retry-After` HTTP-date headers are ignored in both the guarded provider fetch path and the ChatGPT Responses retry sleep path, while valid obsolete RFC 850 years inside the 50-year window still resolve as future retry dates.
- Focused implementation proof at `6481c1c792e07cad2fa394d26e649eed2dc7ad4a`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-transport-fetch.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts` passed with 2 Vitest shards, 29 `packages/ai` tests, and 91 `src/agents` tests.
- Current-head CI proof at `def9d3dcfce1bcee11cf6a4a38bebca8e4f5e07e`: `Real behavior proof`, `Scan changed paths (precise)`, `check-lint`, `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`, `build-artifacts`, and the full CI check rollup passed; the previous `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` timeout passed on the refreshed head.
- Current-head diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed after merging current `upstream/main`, and the PR three-dot diff remains limited to the four Retry-After source/test files.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD` passed on the implementation commit with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: `Sun, 31 Feb 2027 00:00:00 GMT` and `Sunday, 31-Feb-27 00:00:00 GMT` are treated as malformed, and `Sunday, 06-Nov-50 00:00:00 GMT` resolves through the RFC 850 50-year future window.
- Provider-stub transcript at `def9d3dcfce1bcee11cf6a4a38bebca8e4f5e07e`:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-transport-fetch.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose -t retry-after` passed: `26 passed | 65 skipped`; covered `buildGuardedModelFetch > long retry-after handling`, including `ignores invalid HTTP-date retry-after values: Sun, 31 Feb 2027 00:00:00 GMT`, `ignores invalid HTTP-date retry-after values: Sunday, 31-Feb-27 00:00:00 GMT`, and `interprets RFC 850 retry-after years within the 50-year future window`.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-transport-fetch.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose -t Retry-After` passed: `6 passed | 23 skipped` for `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`; covered `streamOpenAICodexResponses transport`, including both malformed February headers and `honors RFC 850 Retry-After years within the 50-year future window`.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of chat.postMessage
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: `pnpm test`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: clean up queued chat turns on abort
target.body:
Closes #102914

AI-assisted: yes

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where queued chat followup turns could remain in Gateway memory when the owning abort signal fired before queue completion. This affected the queued chat/followup lifecycle and could leave stale run identities in `chatQueuedTurns` until the turn was otherwise processed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now attaches a once-only abort listener when a queued chat turn is registered. The listener removes only the exact current queued entry that still owns cancellation, so stale listeners cannot remove a reused run id and retired collect-mode entries remain as idempotency guards until aggregate completion.

## User Impact

Gateway queued chat turns clean up promptly after owner aborts without allowing duplicate dispatches for retired collect entries. This reduces stale in-memory queue state while preserving existing idempotency behavior.

## Evidence

Real Gateway queue behavior proof from the production queue module, run against PR head `3aecbe6bf2e443db0cff0ab4df473293dbb3fe80`:


The proof script imported `registerQueuedChatTurn`, `retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation`, `completeQueuedChatTurn`, and `getQueuedChatTurn` from `src/gateway/chat-queued-turns.ts`, then exercised the runtime queue map directly. It shows the queued turn is registered, the owner abort signal fires, the entry is removed, stale aborts do not remove reused run ids, and retired collect identities survive abort until completion.

## What Problem This Solves

Slack message tool `delete`/`react`/`remove-reaction`/etc. actions fail with `channel_not_found` because the channel ID is lowercased during target resolution before being passed to the Slack Web API. Slack channel IDs are case-sensitive (C0BG72N6Z0V vs c0bg72n6z0v), and the lowercased form is rejected.

The root cause is in `resolveActionTarget`: after resolving `channelId` through the target resolver, the normalized result (which lowercases the entire `kind:id` string) always overwrites the original `channelId` -- even when the resolution was just case normalization with no directory/plugin match.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.ts | Only overwrite `channelId` when `resolutionSource !== "normalized"`. Pure normalization (prefix + lowercase, no directory/plugin match) does not carry canonical ID information, so the raw input is preserved for the plugin's own case-preserving parser. |

target.title: fix(codex): route internal heartbeat sends through provider

Closes #102206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server heartbeat/internal turns could be stamped as `webchat`-bound, causing Discord notification sends from those internal turns to be rejected by the default cross-provider outbound policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex message-tool routing should still prefer the explicit message channel for normal deliverable turns, but the internal `webchat` channel is only a non-delivery source marker for heartbeat-style turns. When Codex receives both `messageChannel: "webchat"` and a deliverable `messageProvider`, this change binds message-tool execution to the deliverable provider instead of the internal marker.

## User Impact

Codex-backed heartbeat notifications can send to the intended provider without requiring users to loosen cross-provider messaging settings globally.

## Evidence

- Deterministic source-level reproduction: current main can pass the internal Codex `webchat` marker as the effective `messageProvider` for heartbeat/internal turns, which leaves Discord-targeted sends subject to the webchat provider policy. The added regression test builds a Codex dynamic-tool context with `messageChannel: "webchat"` and `messageProvider: "discord"` and asserts outbound sends are routed through Discord instead of the internal marker.

target.title: fix(ai): normalize Azure deployment map lookups
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #102936.

Azure OpenAI deployment maps are keyed by model id, but the resolver currently does an exact-case lookup and reparses the map on every call. A configured entry such as `GPT-4o=Prod-East` can be missed when runtime code asks for `gpt-4O`, causing the Azure request to fall back to the raw model id instead of the configured deployment name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deployment map is shared by the package provider and embedded OpenAI transport path, so the normalization belongs in the shared helper rather than either caller.

## User Impact

Azure OpenAI users can use deployment-map model ids without having to match casing exactly, while deployment names keep their original casing and existing fallback behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- Cache the most recent parsed deployment map so repeated resolution does not rebuild it for every call.
- Resolve model ids case-insensitively by lowercasing map keys only for lookup.
- Add regression coverage for mixed-case model ids and deployment-name preservation.

## Evidence

- Deterministic source-level reproduction: before this change, `parseAzureDeploymentMap()` stored map keys exactly as configured and `resolveAzureDeploymentForModel()` used an exact-case `Map.get(model)` lookup, so `GPT-4o=prod-east` did not resolve when the runtime model id arrived as `gpt-4O`. The added regression test asserts mixed-case configured/runtime ids now resolve to the configured Azure deployment name.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/azure-deployment-map.test.ts` — 1 file passed, 3 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/azure-openai-responses.test.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` — 2 shards passed; 304 tests passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Diff secret scan for API-key/token/private-key patterns — no potential secrets in diff.

Note: I did not run a live Azure request because no Azure OpenAI deployment credentials are available in this environment. `pnpm check:changed -- packages/ai/src/providers/azure-deployment-map.ts packages/ai/src/providers/azure-deployment-map.test.ts` could not run locally because the repo delegated to Blacksmith Testbox and the local `crabbox` binary failed its basic `--version/--help` sanity check before executing checks.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102933 — `parseXmlishPlainTextToolCallBlockAt` and
`parseXmlishPlainTextToolCallBlockEndAt` reject function calls with zero
parameters (e.g. `<function=get_system_info></function>`) by returning `null`
when `parameterCount === 0`. This prevents tool-call-repair from recognizing
or repairing any XML-ish tool calls that do not take arguments.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two `parameterCount === 0` guard clauses were overly conservative. The
existing close-tag validation (`consumeXmlishFunctionClose`) already
guarantees that a `</function>` delimiter is present before the block is
accepted. Removing the parameter count check allows zero-parameter calls to
reach the close-tag validator, which correctly handles the empty-body case.

## User Impact

**Before:** `<function=get_system_info></function>` → `parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks` returns `null`
**After:** Same input → returns `[{ name: "get_system_info", arguments: {} }]`

target.title: fix(agents): resolveMessagePrefix now checks channel and account messagePrefix configs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `resolveMessagePrefix` helper only checked the global `messages.messagePrefix` config, ignoring channel-specific and account-specific overrides. Operators could not set per-channel or per-account message prefixes, even though `ackReaction` and `responsePrefix` both correctly cascaded through all four levels.

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/identity.ts`, `resolveMessagePrefix` accepted `configured` and `hasAllowFrom` options but lacked the `channel` and `accountId` parameters. Additionally, `resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig` only passed `channel` + `accountId` to `resolveResponsePrefix`, not to `resolveMessagePrefix`. The WhatsApp caller `buildInboundLine` also omitted `accountId`, so even after the resolver supported it, account-level `messagePrefix` would never be selected in the real production path.

## Changes

### Core fix ([src/agents/identity.ts](src/agents/identity.ts))

Implement the same L1-L4 precedence cascade used by `resolveResponsePrefix` and `resolveAckReaction`:

1. **L1**: Channel account level (`channels[X].accounts[Y].messagePrefix`)
2. **L2**: Channel level (`channels[X].messagePrefix`)
3. **L3**: Global messages level (`messages.messagePrefix`) or caller-configured option
4. **L4**: `hasAllowFrom` → identity name prefix → fallback (`"[openclaw]"`)

### WhatsApp callers

- **message-line.ts**: Changed to passing `channel: "whatsapp"` + `accountId` — full L1-L4 cascade resolved internally
- **message-line.runtime.ts**: WhatsApp runtime copy updated with same L1-L4 cascade
- **process-message.ts**: Passes `params.route.accountId` through to `buildInboundLine`

### Tests

25 new tests in `identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts` covering backward compatibility, channel-level, account-level, full cascade, and `resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig` integration. All existing WhatsApp inbound-line tests (23/23) pass unchanged.

## Evidence

### Caller-path proof: `buildInboundLine` with account-level `messagePrefix`

```
$ npx tsx scripts/verify-102937-caller.ts
HEAD: ea3500ff

buildInboundLine output:
[WhatsApp +1555 Wed 2023-11-15 06:13:20 GMT+8] +1555: [Biz-Account] Hello from customer

✓ channel prefix NOT leaked: correctly absent
```

Harness imports the real `buildInboundLine`, sets up `channels.whatsapp.accounts.business.messagePrefix: "[Biz-Account]"`, and verifies the account prefix actually appears in the formatted inbound line. Channel prefix is confirmed NOT leaked when account prefix is set.

### Resolver proof: `resolveMessagePrefix` L1-L4 cascade

```
✓ L1→L2 fallback: "[WA-Channel]"

✓ L2 empty: ""
✓ L3 global: "[Global]"
```

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of chat.postMessage
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: `pnpm test`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
- `CI=true pnpm oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/send.ts extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts extensions/slack/src/blocks.test-helpers.ts`
- `CI=true pnpm vitest run extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts` (15 tests)
- `CI=true pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `git diff --check`

## Verification
- Thread-scoped progress chrome converts to `reactions.add` instead of `chat.postMessage`.
- Progress chrome without a reaction target is suppressed before Slack post.
- Semantic replies using the same leading emoji remain sendable.

target.title: fix(workshop): keep approval target names UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop lifecycle approvals bound the `Target skill:` line to the 512-UTF-16-code-unit approval-description limit with raw JavaScript `slice`. If an astral character crossed that exact cut, the prompt contained a lone surrogate and could render `�` instead of a valid target name.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildLifecycleApprovalDescription` is the source formatter for apply, reject, and quarantine approval payloads. This change replaces only its raw target-name slice with the existing shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`.

That is the best owner boundary: proposal lookup, lifecycle policy, persistence, gateway limits, and renderers remain unchanged, while every affected approval payload becomes valid before it leaves the formatter. Downstream UI or gateway sanitization would be later, duplicated, and incomplete.

The regression exercises the real `proposeCreateSkill` → persisted proposal → `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval` path. It extends the existing metadata-bound test instead of adding a near-duplicate scenario, preserves every required approval fact, checks the shared 512-unit constant, and rejects lone high or low surrogates.

The docs correction changes the generic plugin approval description limit from the stale 256 value to the runtime and gateway-protocol value of 512.

## User Impact

Operators see a clean ellipsis-truncated target name for long Unicode skill names. Short names, approval policy, allowed decisions, timeout behavior, proposal lookup/state, and apply/reject/quarantine behavior do not change.

## Evidence

Frozen reviewed head: `3e7224efcbcfb8f23f16e4ba44ee10c4f78b8c49`.

Untrusted contributor code was exercised only in sanitized AWS Crabbox leases with public networking, no Tailscale, no instance role, isolated `HOME`, pinned Node/pnpm, `--fresh-pr`, and `--no-hydrate`.

- [Exact-final-head non-test Node behavior proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e069f47836f4) on AWS lease `cbx_94657e95da1f`: created persisted boundary and short-control proposals, resolved the exported approval payload, and checked the behavior contract without Vitest. Boundary output was at most 512 UTF-16 code units, kept the complete prefix plus one ellipsis, contained every approval fact, and had no unpaired surrogate; the short control remained unchanged.
- [Focused GREEN](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c6f44a064850): `pnpm test src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts` — 1 file, 4/4 tests passed.
- [Old-slice RED](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6b0823018ad0): in a fresh checkout, restoring only the old raw `slice` made exactly the boundary regression fail; the received target line contained `�` before the ellipsis.
- [Full Workshop GREEN](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_b55a74f632ba): `pnpm test src/skills/workshop` — 2 files, 40/40 tests passed.
- [Exact-final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29033553042): success; 44 jobs succeeded and 11 skipped. The complete PR rollup is 65 success, 38 skipped, 1 neutral, 2 cancelled stale automation runs, and 0 pending/failing.
- [OpenGrep attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29033553021): success after retrying the first attempt's GitHub-release lookup/SARIF infrastructure failure.
- Source-blind behavior validation: PASS — 11/11 contract clauses, no accepted findings or evidence gaps.
- Fresh full-branch autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings, correctness confidence 0.88. Independent exact-head review also found no blocker.
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/plugins/plugin-permission-requests.md`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

No external service participates in this formatter path. Browser UI automation was not used; the live proof observes the exported approval payload consumed by the approval runtime/UI.

## Root Cause and Provenance

The raw bounded slice was introduced in #100498 (`f53103de72da09185b27a58618ece136a5667c18`). JavaScript string indices are UTF-16 code units, so the cut could land between a valid high/low surrogate pair. This PR follows the same shared-helper fix class as #102816 but covers the distinct Skill Workshop approval formatter. A live related-PR search found no same-point open fix.

## Risk / Compatibility

Risk is low and display-only. At a pair-splitting boundary, the visible prefix can be one code unit shorter so the astral character is omitted whole before the existing ellipsis. There are no config, schema, storage, protocol, dependency, provider, security-boundary, or operator-workflow changes.

Landed through the repository native wrapper as `b451d8b5e59539c21009947c23e203df7d438943` after exact-head Testbox preparation and merge verification.

target.title: [AI-assisted] Preserve thread sessions across daily reset by default
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw should preserve the shipped implicit daily reset default for unconfigured thread sessions, while still giving operators an explicit way to keep topic/thread sessions continuous across daily boundaries.

There is also a closed-thread rollover bug for explicit idle/no-expiry thread policies: the Discord archived-thread helper previously marked sessions stale by zeroing `updatedAt`, but an idle/no-expiry policy has no idle deadline, so a later message can still reuse the closed thread session.

## Fix

- Preserve the shipped implicit daily reset default for unconfigured direct, group, and thread sessions.
- Document explicit topic/thread continuity with `session.resetByType.thread: { mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 0 }`.
- Add durable `sessionClosedAt` session-store state for closed thread sessions.
- Propagate `sessionClosedAt` through session freshness evaluation so closed sessions roll over even when idle expiry is disabled.
- Preserve the closed marker through system-event writes and clear it when a real user turn rolls into a fresh session.

## Evidence

Current-head proof after closed-marker consistency fix:

- **Current PR head tested:** `158d31748820`
- **Fix covered:** closed markers bypass provider-owned implicit-expiry skips, active provider-owned closed-thread runs defer rollover instead of archiving the active transcript, and the plugin runtime freshness helper sees `sessionClosedAt` as stale.
- **Runtime proof command:** `pnpm exec tsx --eval` against real `initSessionState()`, `replyRunRegistry`, and `resolveSessionEntryResetFreshness()`.
- **Focused acceptance command:** `CI=true node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts src/config/sessions/entry-freshness.test.ts src/config/sessions/sessions.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-session-close.test.ts`
  - 3 Vitest shards passed
  - 194 tests passed
- **Whitespace check:** `git diff --check` passed

```json

      "state": "stale",

    },

      "isNewSession": false,
      "reusedPrevious": true,
      "previousSessionEntry": null,

```

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #102910 — `splitTelegramHtmlChunks` throws when HTML tag overhead fills chunk, causing outbound delivery (outbound-adapter.ts) to fail. The fix strips rich formatting and retries as bounded plain text, so message content is delivered within the chunk limit. ## Why This Change Was Made In `appendText`, the `available <= 0 && !chunkHasPayload` branch previously threw. The fix clears `openTags`, sets a fallback flag, and resets — retrying as plain text. A guard in the main loop skips orphan close tags so no unopened fragments leak in. The existing `send.ts`/`rich-message.ts` try-catch fallback paths are preserved. ## User Impact **Before:** nested formatting + small limit = throw = outbound failure **After:** same input = bounded plain text, content delivered ## Evidence Branch: `fix/102910-telegram-tag-overhead` | Base: `upstream/main` | Node: v22.19.0 Linux x64 ### Outbound delivery path proof `splitTelegramHtmlChunks` is the chunker for `chunkTelegramOutboundText` (outbound-adapter.ts:56) and `buildChunkedTextPlan` (send.ts:954): ``` Input: x limit=10 Before fix: throws Error After fix: ["x"] Bounded (len<=10): PASS Content delivered: PASS No orphan close tags: PASS Normal path unchanged: PASS ``` ### Regression tests 68 passed, 1 test file ### Checks - oxfmt — passed - oxlint — passed - git diff --check — passed - autoreview --engine claude — **patch is correct (0.95)**, no findings ### Diff format.ts: +19 (flag + tag-strip + orphan-close skip) format.test.ts: +5 (verify bounded plain-text delivery) - [x] I understand what the code does - [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(slack): keep mpDM human and bot messages on one group session
target.body:
Fixes #102676

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running multiple Slack agents in one multi-party DM (mpDM) would get **two parallel sessions per agent** for the same room: human messages keyed as `slack:group:<id>`, while bot-authored messages (often missing `channel_type`) fell back to C-prefix inference and keyed as `slack:channel:<id>` when channel info could not be resolved. That split context breaks `/reset` and produces stale twin-session replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper and maintainer feedback asked for carrying/caching **authoritative** Slack conversation type (`channel_type: "mpim"` / `conversations.info` `is_mpim`) through the unresolved bot-event path—not G-prefix heuristics alone (closed #102702 / #102752).

This change keeps a process-local authoritative type cache separate from the name/topic channel cache so remembering type does not skip later name fetches. On `conversations.info` failure, `resolveChannelName` still surfaces a previously remembered type so ingress classification stays consistent.

Non-goals: historical twin-session doctor migration; live multi-bot bot-authored path was validated at source level; live proof below is human-authored C-prefix Group DM session keying on a real Slack workspace.

## User Impact

mpDM rooms keep **one session key family** (`slack:group:<id>`) for turns in that room. Private/public channels remain `slack:channel:<id>`.

## Evidence

### 1. Live Slack (real workspace) — redacted

Environment: local macOS gateway on PR head `59908fbec`, Socket Mode Slack app in workspace `macmini-claw`, bot `openclaw`.

**Control (public/private channel, not mpDM):**
```
Inbound app_mention ... channel:C0AL6DKA70U ... (channel, ...)
session: agent:main:slack:channel:c0al6dka70u
```

**Target (Group DM / C-prefix modern mpDM, two human accounts + bot):**
```
watch-mpdm result:
  GROUP agent:main:slack:group:c0bge2wsml4
  CHANNEL agent:main:slack:channel:c0al6dka70u [IGNORED old]
---- RESULT: got_group_session ----
```

Gateway runtime (redacted):
```
lane=session:agent:main:slack:group:c0bge2wsml4
[slack] delivered reply to channel:C0BGE2WSML4
```

Channel probe: Slack `connected=true`, `healthState=healthy`, bot `openclaw` present.

Note: model reply returned Deepseek 401 (invalid API key) — unrelated to session keying; the **session key** is the proof target and is correctly `slack:group:` for the Group DM.

### 2. Focused source regression

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.test.ts -t "102676"
✓ keeps C-prefixed mpDM human and bot-authored ingress on one group session when channel info fails (#102676)
✓ does not reclassify unresolved G-prefix private channels as mpDM group sessions (#102676)
```

Full prepare suite: 116 passed. oxlint/oxfmt clean on touched files.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Live C-prefix Slack Group DM (mpDM-class room id `C0BGE2WSML4`) keys as `agent:main:slack:group:c0bge2wsml4`, distinct from a real channel room which keys as `slack:channel:c0al6dka70u`.
- Environment: macOS local OpenClaw gateway (PR `59908fbec`), Slack Socket Mode, workspace macmini-claw, bot openclaw; Group DM with two human accounts + bot.
- Current-main contrast: Without correct type resolution/cache, C-prefix rooms without explicit `mpim` fall to `channel` session keys; the live channel control still shows `slack:channel:`, while the Group DM on this patch shows `slack:group:`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Configure Slack socket mode; run gateway on this branch.
  2. Open Slack Group DM (two humans + openclaw bot; no #channel).
  3. Send a human message in that Group DM.
  4. `pnpm openclaw sessions --active 60` / watch script → observe `slack:group:c0bge2wsml4`.
- Evidence after fix: Session list shows `GROUP agent:main:slack:group:c0bge2wsml4`; gateway lane `session:agent:main:slack:group:c0bge2wsml4`; delivery to `C0BGE2WSML4`.
- Control check: Earlier #channel @mention created only `slack:channel:c0al6dka70u` and remains separate; Group DM did not land on `slack:channel:` for `C0BGE2WSML4`.
- Observed result after fix: Live Group DM uses **group** session family as required for mpDM; channel control remains channel-keyed.
- What was not tested: Live multi-bot bot-authored twin-session race under failed `conversations.info` (covered by focused unit tests); historical twin migration; Discord noise unrelated.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Code and tests should be reviewed as contributor-owned.

target.title: fix(skills): preserve compact prompt descriptions
target.body:
Related: #50677

## What Problem This Solves

When a skills catalog exceeded `maxSkillsPromptChars`, OpenClaw's compact fallback removed every description. Opaque skill names then lost the semantic trigger guidance the model needs to choose the right skill.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compact formatter now preserves the existing name/location/version identity set first, then spends only the remaining prompt budget on bounded descriptions. Description truncation reuses the shared UTF-16-safe helper so a limit cannot split a surrogate pair, and the prompt-format version advances so persisted sessions rebuild the changed catalog shape.

This is a current-`main` rewrite of the original contribution: it keeps the newer version-marker/session-refresh behavior, accounts for the complete rendered notice when enforcing the cap, and avoids trading an identity for description text.

## User Impact

Large skills installations retain useful matching descriptions whenever budget remains. At the exact identity-only budget, behavior remains the previous compact contract: all identities fit, descriptions are omitted, and the prompt explains that state. Documentation now describes both compact modes.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head: `3bf7b9967330af23b8db52c175192442da3cf178`.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox focused run `run_3ff6ad25c73e`: 2 files, 31 tests passed (`compact-format` and session snapshot coverage).
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox changed-surface run `run_1eeb815a2313`: core/core-tests/docs lanes passed, including core and core-test tsgo, changed-file lint, import-cycle and repository guards.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox live run `run_b4518917d9ec`: two real `openclaw agent --local` turns through the repository mock `/v1/responses` endpoint. At 18,000 chars, 29 discovered identities/versions and all 12 long fixture descriptions survived with UTF-16-safe truncation. At the exact 6,107-char identity budget, the same 29 identities/versions remained byte-for-byte after description-line removal, with zero descriptions.
- Local fallback: focused tests passed (31/31), touched files formatted, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview on the final source diff: clean; no accepted or actionable findings.

AI-assisted maintainer takeover: an OpenClaw maintainer agent rebased and rewrote the contributor patch against current `main`, added regression/live proof, and preserved contributor credit in the commit.

target.title: feat(durable): add opt-in workflow worker loop
target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR5/5 in the durable runtime stack. It follows the threshold-met PR4 schema lifecycle/recovery hardening and adds the opt-in durable workflow worker loop, now wired into the real gateway lifecycle behind explicit durable worker env flags.

## Durable core stack overview

Durable core means the shared, opt-in runtime substrate that records run identity, step/event ordering, parent/child links, bounded refs, recovery states, signals/timers, and read-only inspection for long-running OpenClaw agent/session/task/subagent work. The full stack is: PR1 #101828 RFC/root-cause/boundary; PR2 #102495 durable runtime core; PR3 #102839 agent/session/subagent restart and upgrade-safety proof; PR4 #102943 schema lifecycle/recovery hardening; PR5 #102983 opt-in workflow worker loop.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR5/5.
- Upstream gates: PR1 #101828, PR2 #102495, PR3 #102839, and PR4 #102943 are threshold-met in stack state.
- Current PR5 head: `54964adee1` (`fix(durable): wire opt-in worker recovery`).
- Previous below-threshold head: `41d433a127`.

## Dependency / promotion gate

PR5 is the final durable-stack PR. Stack completion still requires a fresh ClawSweeper/reviewer rating at or above gold shrimp/schrimp on this repaired PR5 head.

## What Problem This Solves

After the durable state model, recovery primitives, restart behavior, and schema lifecycle are accepted, OpenClaw needs a worker loop that can execute durable workflow steps without enabling background automation by default. This PR adds that worker path as explicit opt-in automation and proves expired claims can be reclaimed safely.

## Scope

- Wire `startDurableWorkflowWorkerFromEnv` into the actual gateway run loop after gateway startup, next to durable startup/recovery lifecycle handling.
- Keep worker execution disabled unless both durable workflows and `OPENCLAW_DURABLE_WORKER` are explicitly enabled.
- Reclaim expired claimed runs/steps by allowing `recovery_state = 'claimed'` rows with expired claim TTLs to be selected again.
- Add regression coverage for gateway worker lifecycle, env opt-in behavior, and expired-claim reclaim semantics.

## Non-scope

- Does not broaden durable workflows beyond the existing explicit flag model.
- Does not change PR2 durable core boundaries or PR4 schema lifecycle semantics.
- Does not introduce default background execution for existing installs.

## Base / diff hygiene

- PR5 remains stacked as the final durable PR.
- Repair commit is scoped to `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts`, `src/durable/sqlite-store.ts`, `src/durable/sqlite-store.test.ts`, and `src/durable/worker.test.ts`.
- `git diff --check` passed on repaired head.

## Proof matrix

| Gate | Command / artifact | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Durable worker/store/gateway proof | `pnpm exec vitest run src/durable/*.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts` | passed; 7 files / 27 tests |
| Gateway lifecycle wiring proof | `pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts` | passed; 1 file / 37 tests |
| Typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:core` | passed |
| Diff hygiene | `git diff --check` | passed |
| PR5 local-e live smoke | `/tmp/pr5-local-e-worker-smoke-20260709.json` | passed; disabled-by-default stayed stopped/queued, explicit-enable claimed and completed one seeded local-e workflow step |
| Local-e smoke cleanup | `/tmp/pr5-local-e-worker-smoke-cleanup-20260709.json` | passed; cancelled the intentionally queued disabled smoke row after recording evidence |

## Live proof

Environment inspected first: local-e instance manifest, version lock, launchd plist, local-e config, listening port, and logs were checked before mutation. Persistent launchd config was not edited.

PR5-specific local-e smoke used the repaired PR5 source against `/Users/avo/aicos/.runtime-home/openclaw/instances/local-e/state`:

- Disabled/default behavior: `OPENCLAW_DURABLE_WORKFLOWS=1` without `OPENCLAW_DURABLE_WORKER`; `startDurableWorkflowWorkerFromEnv` returned `running: false`, `stopped: true`, and the seeded local-e workflow step remained `queued` / `runnable`.

- P1 real behavior proof: addressed with PR5-specific local-e smoke artifact showing disabled-by-default and explicit-enable behavior.

## Risk / upgrade notes

- Background execution remains opt-in. Without `OPENCLAW_DURABLE_WORKER`, the gateway startup hook creates only a stopped no-op handle.

target.title: fix(media): accept repeated content-length when values match
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where media and plugin paths that rely on shared Content-Length parsing could reject otherwise valid responses when response headers expose repeated matching Content-Length values as a comma-joined header value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared media parser now parses each comma-separated Content-Length member with the existing digit and safe-integer checks, then accepts the header only when every parsed value agrees. Malformed, unsafe, empty, or conflicting values still fail before body reads, so callers keep their existing byte-cap decisions in one owner-local helper.

## User Impact

Users and plugin/channel developers are less likely to see valid media, auth, or download responses fail solely because an upstream server or proxy repeated an identical Content-Length header. Conflicting or malformed headers are still rejected.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: at current head `3b943a1294cc06c3432ef146022201338540ecb2`, the media fetch caller path accepts a response whose `Content-Length` value is `5, 5`, reads the 5-byte body, and rejects a conflicting `5, 6` value before body handling.
- Media caller-path proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with `readRemoteMediaBuffer` from `src/media/fetch.ts` and fetch-compatible responses passed with this terminal output:

  ```text
  ok repeated matching content-length -> bytes=5 text=hello
  bad conflicting content-length -> MediaFetchError: Failed to fetch media from https://example.com/file.bin: invalid content-length header: 5, 6
  ```

- Focused regression tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/media-core/src/content-length.test.ts src/media/fetch.test.ts` passed: 2 Vitest shards, 44 tests.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` passed with `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`.
- Scope checked: `git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD` contains only `packages/media-core/src/content-length.ts`, `packages/media-core/src/content-length.test.ts`, and `src/media/fetch.test.ts`.

target.title: fix(copilot): redact OAuth error response body in fetchJson error messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

GitHub Copilot OAuth error responses could leak raw response body text into Error
messages. `fetchJson()` called `readProviderTextResponse` on non-2xx responses and
included the raw text verbatim. The shared `extractProviderErrorDetail` function
already handles bounded reads, JSON parsing, structured error extraction, and
`redactSensitiveText` — this PR switches the error path to use it.

Related: #97499 added 16 MiB bounded reads for the success path; this fixes the
remaining leak in the error path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fetchJson()` in `src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts` called `readProviderTextResponse`
on non-2xx responses and embedded the raw body text in the Error message. The fix
replaces it with `extractProviderErrorDetail` from the shared provider-http-errors
module, which redacts sensitive fields and extracts structured error codes.

## User Impact

**Before:** `400 Bad Request: {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"bad code","refresh_token":"ghr_..."}`
**After:** `GitHub Copilot token refresh request failed with status 400: bad code [code=invalid_grant]`

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/copilot-oauth-error-body` | Base: `upstream/main` | Node: v22.19.0 Linux x64

### Live proof: wrapper-level real HTTP server

Local HTTP server returns a 400 error with a synthetic Copilot token error body.
`refreshGitHubCopilotToken` (the changed wrapper) is called and its Error message
is verified to exclude raw JSON keys and tokens:

```

error_description in message: PASS
```

target.title: fix(google): bound SSE stream body reads at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `parseGoogleSseChunks` function in Google's transport stream reads SSE response bodies without a byte cap. A hanging or malicious Google/Vertex AI endpoint that streams data without `\n\n` boundaries (or that never sends `[DONE]`) could cause unbounded buffer growth and OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenClaw codebase already applies 16 MiB byte caps to SSE/NDJSON streams in Ollama (#99585), Mistral, and OpenAI Chat/Responses providers. Google was the last major bundled provider whose raw SSE parser had no such limit. This change applies the same pattern with a matching fail-closed threshold.

## User Impact

A Google Gemini or Vertex AI endpoint that returns an oversized SSE body (or an unbounded event stream) no longer causes unbounded memory growth. The stream errors cleanly with a descriptive message once the 16 MiB limit is exceeded.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts` — 86 tests passed (3 new: mock oversized body, real TCP loopback for Gemini, real TCP loopback for Vertex)
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google/transport-stream.ts extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts` — passed
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google/transport-stream.ts extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts` — exit 0
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` — clean
- Open PR collision check: searched open PRs touching `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts` — none found

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Google and Vertex AI SSE success-body streams are capped at 16 MiB.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; real `node:http` loopback servers.

Exact command run after this patch:
```
pnpm test extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts
  ✓ 86 tests passed
```

Three layers of proof:

1. **Mock oversized body** — feeds a 16 MiB + 1 byte single-chunk SSE event through a mocked `buildGuardedModelFetch` response; verifies `stopReason: "error"` with the overflow message.

2. **Real Gemini TCP loopback** — starts a real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0` that responds with a 16 MiB + 1 byte SSE body; the transport stream fetches through `globalThis.fetch` from this real server; verifies the byte guard triggers on real network bytes.

3. **Real Vertex TCP loopback** — same real server setup through the Vertex transport stream with `gcp-vertex-credentials` auth marker; verifies the guard also fires on the Vertex routing path.

All three tests assert `stopReason: "error"` and an error message containing `"exceeds 16777216 bytes"`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

- Wire signed marketplace feed profiles into hosted catalog refresh using the signed envelope verifier and configured threshold.

target.title: Apply Claw update reconciliations
target.body:
## Summary

- Implements the consent-gated mutating side of the Claws update/reconcile track from [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27), stacked after [#102959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102959).
- Allows `claws update <claw> --from <manifest> --yes` to revalidate the dry-run plan, install supported target artifacts, reconcile artifact provenance refs, update managed workspace/persona files, and remove stale unchanged managed workspace files.
- Keeps unsafe cases fail-closed: required blockers, target diagnostics, manual workspace edits, missing `--workspace` for workspace updates, stale removal errors, and workspace write conflicts all stop the mutating update.

## Stack

[RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) -> [#101328 validation/dry-run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) -> [#101755 apply/provenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755) -> [#101973 workspace/persona apply](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101973) -> [#102228 plugin installers/uninstall warnings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102228) -> [#102296 status/remove](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102296) -> [#102306 export/creation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102306) -> [#102383 skill artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102383) -> [#102406 MCP artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102406) -> [#102427 doctor diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102427) -> [#102959 update dry-run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102959) -> this PR

## Behavior

`claws update --dry-run` remains the read-only planning surface from #102959. This PR adds the `--yes` path:

1. read and validate the target manifest
2. rebuild the update plan and fail on not found, blocked, manual, or diagnostic states
3. require `--workspace` when the reconcile plan includes workspace/persona entries
4. validate target workspace writes before artifact mutation
5. install supported target artifacts
6. remove stale managed workspace files only when unchanged, retaining modified files
7. write/update target workspace files
8. persist the final target artifact provenance with stale Claw refs removed
9. emit `openclaw.clawUpdateResult.v1`

Notably, artifact provenance is not advanced until workspace reconciliation succeeds, so a failed update does not make `claws status` report the target version or target artifact refs.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts src/claws/update-plan.test.ts src/claws/provenance.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/provenance.test.ts src/claws/artifact-installers.test.ts src/claws/workspace.test.ts src/claws/lifecycle-state.test.ts src/claws/update-plan.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.uninstall.test.ts src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts src/claws/doctor.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts src/cli/program/root-command-descriptions.test.ts`
- `git diff --check && node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs && pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/cli/claws-cli.runtime.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts src/claws/lifecycle-state.ts src/claws/provenance.ts src/claws/update-plan.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/tsgo --noEmit --pretty false` reaches inherited `src/secrets/config-io.ts(12,17)` TS4058 after this patch's local type issue was fixed.
- `codex review -c model=gpt-5.5 --uncommitted` reported no actionable correctness issues after fixes for same-id workspace moves, deferred provenance persistence, and the update-result logger type.

## Real behavior proof

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "openclaw.clawUpdateResult.v1",
  "clawVersion": "2.0.0",
  "updateSummary": {
    "totalEntries": 2,
    "added": 0,

  "oldExists": false
}
```

target.title: fix(gateway): use regex instead of per-character loop in chat input sanitizer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102915 — `stripDisallowedChatControlChars` uses a per-character `for...of` loop with `output += char` string concatenation. For large messages (1MB+), this blocks the gateway event loop for ~120ms on every `chat.send` request. At 10MB, the block exceeds 750ms — a gateway availability concern.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the per-character loop with `String.prototype.replace` using a precompiled regex. The character class `[\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F\x7F]` matches exactly the same disallowed bytes as the original `if` condition.

## Evidence

### Production-path proof

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { sanitizeChatSendMessageInput } from './src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.js';
const text = 'a'.repeat(1_000_000);
const t0 = performance.now();
const result = sanitizeChatSendMessageInput(text);
console.log('elapsed=' + (performance.now() - t0).toFixed(1) + 'ms  ok=' + result.ok + '  len=' + result.message.length);"

elapsed=7.7ms  ok=true  len=1000000
```

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts -t "sanitizeChatSendMessageInput"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts -t "sanitizeChatSendMessageInput" --reporter=verbose
 ✓ sanitizeChatSendMessageInput > rejects null bytes
 ✓ sanitizeChatSendMessageInput > strips unsafe control characters while preserving tab/newline/carriage return
 ✓ sanitizeChatSendMessageInput > normalizes unicode to NFC
 ✓ sanitizeChatSendMessageInput > completes within 50ms for a 1MB message without control characters
```

### Correctness: all 256 code points match

```
$ node -e "
const oldStrip = (m) => { let o=''; for(const c of m){ const code=c.charCodeAt(0); if(code===9||code===10||code===13||(code>=32&&code!==127)) o+=c; } return o; };
const newStrip = (m) => m.replace(/[\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F\x7F]/g, '');
for(let i=0;i<256;i++){ const input=String.fromCharCode(i); if(oldStrip(input)!==newStrip(input)){ console.log('FAIL at',i); process.exit(1); } }
console.log('All 256 code points match');
"
All 256 code points match
```

### Files Changed (3 files, +19/-8)

```
 src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.ts                   | 10 +++++-----
 src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts    | 10 ++++++++++
 test/scripts/lint-suppressions.test.ts               |  1 +
```

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint after inbound admission gates pass. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

Backfilled sender labels use stable Mattermost user ids instead of per-post user lookups, keeping recovery bounded to the thread fetch path.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without repeated thread-history requests or extra user lookup delays on normal same-session follow-ups.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.test.ts`: 100 passed; covers stable `route.sessionKey`, stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, failed-fetch no-retry, reset-session refetch, dropped pre-admission posts, and bounded backfill without sender enrichment.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.test.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Live proof: local Docker Mattermost Team Edition 10.11.21 at `http://localhost:8065`, with tokens and Mattermost ids redacted. The proof used real Mattermost REST auth, posts, and `/api/v4/posts/<root>/thread` through `monitorMattermostProvider`; a fake websocket only injected `posted` events into the monitor. The route/thread session key stayed stable while the stored thread `sessionId` rotated. Cold start included prior root/thread context, same-session server-only context stayed absent, and stored-thread-session reset included new server-only prior context:

```json
{
  "mattermost": "10.11.21 local Docker, token/id redacted",
  "routeSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKeyStable": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIds": [
    "stored-session-before-reset",
    "stored-session-after-reset"
  ],
  "dispatchCount": 3,
  "firstColdStartContainsPriorThreadContext": true,
  "firstColdStartContainsRootContext": true,
  "sameSessionSkippedServerOnlyContext": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIdResetContainsNewPriorContext": true
}
```

target.title: fix(voice-call): fail-closed media-stream auth for non-Twilio providers
target.body:
Closes #102837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the voice-call media-stream WebSocket endpoint (`/voice/stream`) accepts an unauthenticated `start` frame for non-Twilio providers (Plivo, Telnyx). Anyone who knows a live provider call ID — leaked via a log line, status callback, or prior participation — can connect a WebSocket, inject forged audio into the agent pipeline, and receive the agent's outbound audio.

Only the Twilio provider path enforced the signed per-call stream token. This is the residual half of the previously reported authentication gap (#7001) which was closed for Twilio only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `shouldAcceptStream` callback in `VoiceCallWebhookServer.initializeMediaStreaming` (`webhook.ts:363`) used a hardcoded `this.provider.name === "twilio"` branch to gate token validation, and fell through to `return true` for every other provider. This made the media-stream endpoint permissive for any non-Twilio provider with an active call.

The fix:

1. **`VoiceCallProvider` interface** (`base.ts`) — Declares an optional `isValidStreamToken?(callId, token)` method so any provider can plug in its own per-call credential verification.

2. **`shouldAcceptStream` callback** (`webhook.ts:363`) — Replaces the Twilio-only check with a fail-closed dispatch: if the active provider exposes `isValidStreamToken`, it is called; if not, the stream is **rejected**. Previously the default was `return true` (accept).

Non-goal: This PR does not add per-call stream token generation or validation to Plivo or Telnyx. Telnyx already uses the separate realtime handler path (`realtime-handler.ts`) with its own `consumeStreamToken` UUID-based authentication. Plivo media-stream support can be added with provider-owned credential logic in a follow-up.

## User Impact

Before: A `start` frame with any active call ID and no token was accepted for Plivo or Telnyx media streams. After: the media-stream endpoint **rejects** start frames for providers that have not implemented per-call stream token validation. Twilio deployments are unaffected — existing `isValidStreamToken` logic continues to work. Operators of non-Twilio media-stream deployments must now implement `isValidStreamToken` on their provider before `/voice/stream` connections are accepted; this is the correct secure default.

## Evidence

### Root cause confirmation

Source-level reproduction at `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.ts:363` — Twilio-only token check with fall-through to `return true` for any other provider. Codex review confidence: 0.87.

### Real behavior proof

A stand-alone proof script (`fix-102837-real-behavior-proof.mjs`) exercises the production `MediaStreamHandler` class from `extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.ts` with a real local HTTP server (via `http.createServer`), real WebSocket upgrade, and real `handleUpgrade` → `handleStart` pipeline. The `shouldAcceptStream` callback implements the same fail-closed dispatch as `webhook.ts:363`. The `handleUpgrade` routing does not go through `VoiceCallWebhookServer` — it is wired directly to `MediaStreamHandler.handleUpgrade`. The STT provider is stubbed (same approach as `media-stream.test.ts`).

Run: `npx tsx fix-102837-real-behavior-proof.mjs`

```
# BEHAVIOR PROOF — voice-call media-stream auth fail-closed (fix for #102837)
# Commit / checkout: (local checkout)
#
# Real environment: local HTTP server, real WebSocket upgrade, real
# MediaStreamHandler (production class), real shouldAcceptStream callback
# with the same fail-closed logic as webhook.ts, stub STT provider.
#

[MediaStream] Stream started: MZ-001 (call: CA-001)
[MediaStream] Rejecting stream for unknown call: CA-001
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1008, reason: Unknown call)

[MediaStream] Stream started: MZ-002 (call: CA-002)
[MediaStream] Rejecting stream for unknown call: CA-002
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1008, reason: Unknown call)

[MediaStream] Stream started: MZ-003 (call: CA-003)
[MediaStream] Rejecting stream for unknown call: CA-003
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1008, reason: Unknown call)

[MediaStream] Stream started: MZ-004 (call: CA-004)
[MediaStream] Rejecting stream for unknown call: CA-004
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1008, reason: Unknown call)

[MediaStream] Stream started: MZ-005 (call: CA-005)
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1005, reason: none)
[MediaStream] Stream stopped: MZ-005

# --- Results ---
#
  provider=mock(no-validator)         token=<none>    -> accepted=false close={"code":1008,"reason":"Unknown call"}
  provider=mock(validator-reject)     token=forged    -> accepted=false close={"code":1008,"reason":"Unknown call"}
  provider=mock(validator-accept)     token=<none>    -> accepted=false close={"code":1008,"reason":"Unknown call"}
  provider=mock(validator-accept)     token=forged    -> accepted=false close={"code":1008,"reason":"Unknown call"}
  provider=mock(validator-accept)     token=valid     -> accepted=true sessions=1 close=null

#
# Summary
#
#  PASS: All 5 scenarios match expected security behavior.
```

| Scenario | Result | Meaning |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `mock(no-validator)` + no token | ❌ Rejected (1008) | Fail-closed: provider without `isValidStreamToken` is rejected |
| `mock(validator-reject)` + forged | ❌ Rejected (1008) | Validator returning `false` is rejected |
| `mock(validator-accept)` + no token | ❌ Rejected (1008) | Validator requires token but none given |
| `mock(validator-accept)` + forged | ❌ Rejected (1008) | Validator rejects forged token |
| `mock(validator-accept)` + valid | ✅ Accepted | Validator accepts correct token → session established |

### Unit tests

All 4 test suites pass (88 tests):

```
pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.test.ts        — 46 passed
pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.test.ts   — 22 passed
pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/providers/telnyx.test.ts — 16 passed
pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/providers/plivo.test.ts   —  4 passed
```

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using opencode with review by the author.

target.title: fix(ui): prevent heredoc body content from being parsed as commands (#102875)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102875: The tool-status footer was rendering heredoc body content (e.g., email body text) as failed commands, confusing operators and causing false incident reports.

**Example:** When an agent ran:
```bash
cat > file.txt <<EOF
Buenos dias equipo;
se ajusta la orden A1251718: sc-carwhi(100)
Gracias.
EOF
./scripts/send
```

The Telegram footer showed:
```
⚠️ 🛠 create folder → show > → run sc-carwhi(100) → Gracias. failed
```

Operators interpreted this as a broken/hallucinating agent, when the turn actually succeeded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `scanTopLevelChars` function in `src/agents/tool-display-exec-shell.ts:240` tracked quotes but not heredocs, so semicolons and other shell metacharacters inside heredoc bodies were incorrectly treated as command separators.

## User Impact

- ✅ Heredoc body content no longer appears as phantom failed commands
- ✅ Operators see accurate command summaries
- ✅ No information leak of heredoc payload content in collapsed tool results

## Evidence

### Unit Tests
```
✓ All 48 tests in src/agents/tool-display*.test.ts pass
```

### Manual Verification
```bash
# Test case from issue #102875
resolveExecDetail({ command: `mkdir -p .openclaw/tmp/farm-notices
cat > .openclaw/tmp/farm-notices/ventura.txt <<EOF
Buenos dias equipo;
sc-carwhi(100)
Gracias.
EOF
./scripts/email_preview_new && ./scripts/email_preview_new` })

# Result: "create folder .openclaw/tmp/farm-notices → show > → run email_preview_new → run email_preview_new"
# ✓ No "sc-carwhi(100)" or "Gracias." as separate commands
```

### Files Changed
- `src/agents/tool-display-exec-shell.ts`: +133 lines (heredoc detection and skipping logic)
- `src/agents/tool-display-exec.ts`: +8 lines (collectHeredocTerminators direct scanning)

### Testing Commands
```bash
pnpm test src/agents/tool-display*.test.ts
# Result: Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 48 passed (48)
```

target.title: fix(gateway): reject disallowed browser Origin before accepting auth.mode=none on HTTP (#102834)
target.body:
Closes #102834


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` (documented for trusted-LAN / dev setups) could have state-changing HTTP routes such as `/sessions/<key>/kill`, `/v1/chat/completions`, and `/tools/invoke` reached by cross-origin browser requests from hostile pages. A simple auto-submitting HTML form POST with no custom headers and no `Authorization` header would succeed through the gateway auth gate and reach real business logic, because the HTTP ingress never validated the browser `Origin` header under `auth.mode: "none"`.

Token and password modes are not affected in browser environments (the CORS preflight mechanism blocks `Authorization`-bearing cross-origin requests before they are sent), but this fix adds defense-in-depth on the server side for those modes as well. The WebSocket ingress on the same server was already protected — it checks `Origin` for any client that sends one, regardless of `auth.mode`.

## Why This Change Was Made

A shared browser-Origin gate is applied on the HTTP auth path whenever an `Origin` header is present, before any auth mode (`none`, `token`, `password`, `tailscale`) success return. This mirrors the WebSocket ingress invariant: `enforceOriginCheckForAnyClient` triggers `checkBrowserOrigin` for any `Origin`-bearing client independent of `auth.mode` (see `message-handler.ts:881`).

The gate reuses the existing `browserOriginPolicy` already constructed by `resolveHttpBrowserOriginPolicy` and uses `localDirect` as `isLocalClient` so that legitimate local-loopback clients (e.g. `http://localhost:5173` → `http://127.0.0.1:PORT`) continue to work through the `local-loopback` fallback, matching the WS behavior exactly.

Origin-less requests (headless proxy clients, curl, scripts, OpenAI SDKs) are unaffected — the check is skipped entirely when no `Origin` header is present. The trusted-proxy path, MCP HTTP endpoints, and the WS ingress are all unchanged.

**Scope note**: The gate applies to all auth modes, not just `none`. This is intentional and mirrors the WebSocket side where `enforceOriginCheckForAnyClient` runs regardless of auth mode. For token/password modes, this provides server-side defense-in-depth: standard non-browser API clients (OpenAI SDKs, curl, scripts) never send `Origin` headers, so they are unaffected. Bearer-bearing browser requests from disallowed origins are now rejected even before token comparison, adding a layer of protection against scenarios where a token is obtained by other means (e.g., XSS).

## User Impact

- **Users running `auth.mode: "none"` on loopback** (the documented use case): no change for headless clients; local browsers continue to work via the `local-loopback` origin fallback.
- **Users running `auth.mode: "none"` on LAN** (discouraged by docs): cross-origin browser requests are now rejected unless the origin is explicitly listed in `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`.
- **Token/password/trusted-proxy modes**: no behavioral change for any standard client (OpenAI SDKs, curl, scripts never send `Origin`). Browser-based API clients from disallowed origins are now rejected server-side as defense-in-depth.
- **WebSocket ingress**: no change (already had this protection).

## Evidence

### Unit tests

`src/gateway/auth.test.ts` — four cases covering the fix:

- `rejects HTTP requests with disallowed Origin under auth mode none`
- `accepts HTTP requests with allowed Origin under auth mode none`
- `keeps origin-less HTTP requests working under auth mode none`
- `accepts HTTP requests with local loopback Origin under localDirect auth mode none`

All 240 tests across 3 vitest projects pass with no regressions:

```
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  240 passed (240)
  Duration  4.10s
```

### Real behavior proof

Run `npx tsx fix-102834-real-behavior-proof.mjs` — exercises the actual production `authorizeHttpGatewayConnect` (zero mocks) through the complete `authorizeGatewayConnectCore` path with the patched origin gate:

```
=== Real Behavior Proof: CSRF Origin Check for #102834 ===
Exercising actual authorizeHttpGatewayConnect (patched auth path)

[PASS] auth.mode=none + hostile Origin → reject
       → ok:false, reason=origin_not_allowed
[PASS] auth.mode=none + allowed Origin → accept
       → ok:true
[PASS] auth.mode=none + no Origin → accept (headless)
       → ok:true
[PASS] auth.mode=none + local loopback Origin → accept (local-loopback fallback)
       → ok:true
[PASS] auth.mode=token + hostile Origin → reject (defense-in-depth)
       → ok:false, reason=origin_not_allowed
[PASS] auth.mode=token + no Origin → accept (headless SDK client)
       → ok:true

=== 6 passed, 0 failed ===
```

This script directly imports `authorizeHttpGatewayConnect` from `src/gateway/auth.ts` and runs real requests through the complete auth pipeline including the new `checkBrowserOrigin` gate — no mocks, no test doubles, no server startup.

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: fix(minimax): add timeouts to OAuth HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MiniMax OAuth login could wait indefinitely when either the device-code request or token-poll request accepted the HTTP connection but never returned a response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OAuth flow already has bounded polling and expiry behavior, but each individual outbound HTTP request lacked its own deadline. This change applies one request timeout through both the fetch guard and OAuth abort-signal helper, while preserving the existing PKCE payloads, SSRF hostname policy, error-body limits, and polling loop behavior.

## User Impact

A stalled MiniMax OAuth endpoint no longer leaves the login flow wedged. Authorization-code and token-poll hangs now reject boundedly instead of waiting forever.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/minimax/oauth.test.ts` - passed; `Test Files  1 passed (1)`, `Tests  14 passed (14)`.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/minimax/oauth.ts extensions/minimax/oauth.test.ts` - passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/minimax/oauth.ts extensions/minimax/oauth.test.ts` - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD` - passed; exit 0.
- Open PR collision check: searched open PR topics and scanned the latest 500 open PR changed-file lists; no open PR touched `extensions/minimax/oauth.ts`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: MiniMax OAuth code and token POSTs now have deadlines when the remote endpoint accepts the request but never sends a response.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; real `node:http` loopback server that accepts requests and deliberately never responds. The regression first verifies a bare fetch to the same hanging server remains pending without a deadline.

Exact command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/minimax/oauth.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: the focused tests drive the exported `loginMiniMaxPortalOAuth` path for both the authorization-code request and token-poll request. Each path reaches the local hanging server, carries an `AbortSignal`, and rejects with an abort/timeout-class error within the bounded window.

What was not tested: live MiniMax OAuth traffic; the hang is reproduced with a real local HTTP server, not the real third-party service.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): add timeout to embedding model discovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`discoverEmbeddingModels` in the GitHub Copilot embedding provider calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a `timeoutMs`. A hanging `/models` endpoint can leave the embedding provider adapter stalled during setup, the same class of issue fixed in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC token refresh timeout).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 30s timeout to the Copilot embedding model discovery request so that provider setup fails fast instead of hanging indefinitely when GitHub Copilot's `/models` endpoint stops responding.

## User Impact

Creating the GitHub Copilot embedding provider will time out instead of hanging forever if the model discovery endpoint is unresponsive.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.test.ts
```

Result: `Tests 13 passed (1)`.

The new test asserts that the discovery request is forwarded to `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with `timeoutMs: 30_000`.

### SDK-level real behavior proof

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` honors the `timeoutMs` option. A loopback server that accepts the TCP connection but never sends a byte causes the guarded fetch to reject within the configured timeout:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.timeout-loopback.test.ts
```

(The temporary test file was removed before commit; the command output below is preserved as proof.)

## Real behavior proof

- **Command run:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.timeout-loopback.test.ts`
- **Exact output:** `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 1 passed (1) / Duration ~1.3s`
- **Head SHA:** `79ee01eec72428a72ea3f01fa0caa1bf8e881cca`
- **Environment:** Linux, Node 22.19, local checkout
- **Observed result:** The guarded fetch against the hanging loopback server rejected within `timeoutMs + 2s` and after `timeoutMs - 100ms` with `timeoutMs: 500`.
- **What was not tested:** Live GitHub Copilot `/models` endpoint (no live token).

target.title: fix: normalize unsupported Anthropic inline images
target.body:
Closes #102323

## Summary

- normalize unsupported Anthropic inline image MIME types at the payload boundary instead of forwarding `image/heic` / `image/tiff` verbatim
- keep `@openclaw/ai` package-independent by routing packaged provider normalization through the AI transport host port, with OpenClaw core injecting the shared `src/media/anthropic-inline-images.ts` implementation
- reuse the same normalization path for the packaged Anthropic provider and the custom Anthropic transport
- add regressions for user-image, tool-result image, and text-only/non-vision paths so dropped images are not decoded before filtering

## Verification

- `git diff --check upstream/live-main...HEAD`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check packages/ai/src/host.ts packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts src/llm/ai-transport-host.ts src/media/anthropic-inline-images.ts src/media/image-ops.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`
- `pnpm build`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/live-main`
- `node --import tsx /private/tmp/openclaw-102323-proof-current.ts`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Anthropic user-image and tool-result payloads no longer send unsupported `image/heic` / `image/tiff` media types verbatim; they normalize to `image/jpeg` before the request leaves OpenClaw.
Real environment tested: ran the real `streamAnthropic()` packaged provider from `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` with OpenClaw's AI transport host wiring, plus the real `createAnthropicMessagesTransportStreamFn()` custom transport, against a local `127.0.0.1` loopback Anthropic-compatible capture server that recorded outbound `/v1/messages` payloads and returned Anthropic-style SSE responses.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx /private/tmp/openclaw-102323-proof-current.ts`
Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "captured": [
    { "caseId": "packaged-user-heic", "mediaType": "image/jpeg" },
    { "caseId": "packaged-tool-tiff", "mediaType": "image/jpeg" },
    { "caseId": "transport-user-heic", "mediaType": "image/jpeg" }
  ],
  "packagedResult": { "stopReason": "stop", "errorMessage": "" },
  "packagedToolResult": { "stopReason": "stop", "errorMessage": "" },
  "transportResult": { "stopReason": "stop", "errorMessage": "" }
}
```
Observed result after fix: the packaged Anthropic provider sends both HEIC user images and TIFF tool-result images as `image/jpeg`, and the custom Anthropic transport sends HEIC user images as `image/jpeg`; all three requests completed successfully through the real OpenClaw payload builders.
What was not tested: live `api.anthropic.com` was not called; the proof swaps only the remote endpoint for a loopback capture server, and it does not exercise the wider upstream session/image ingestion paths beyond these Anthropic request builders.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve target agent tool allowlist for subagents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Spawned subagent sessions can lose tools that are allowed only on the target agent profile.

In the GBrain worker-read path, `main` can spawn `dennis-ritchie`, but `main` does not expose `gbrain_readonly`. Dennis has `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`, yet the child session inherits the parent tool allowlist before the target-agent allowlist is persisted. The result is that a fresh Dennis worker does not receive the configured read-only tool even though the target agent configuration allows it.

## Fix

When creating the initial child session patch for `spawnSubagentDirect`, merge inherited tool allow entries from:

- the caller-provided inherited allowlist
- global subagent tool allowlist config: `tools.subagents.tools.alsoAllow`
- target agent config: `targetAgentConfig.tools.alsoAllow`

This keeps the allowlist scoped to the configured target agent instead of broadening the parent or global runtime tool policy.

## Evidence

Current rebased head:

```text
fcaaf7e31139a5ca4be4de43d1b6ca1afffab50f
```

Focused verification after rebasing onto current upstream `main`:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/agents/subagent-spawn.depth-limits.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       86 passed (86)
```

Additional checks:

```text
node --check src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts
git diff --check
```

The new regression coverage exercises `main -> dennis-ritchie` where the parent inherited tool allowlist lacks `gbrain_readonly`, but Dennis' target agent config includes `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`; the persisted child session now retains `gbrain_readonly` in `inheritedToolAllow`.

## Real Runtime Reproduction

On the affected deployment after an approved gateway restart, a fresh real Dennis subagent still failed to receive the tool:

```text
Fresh Dennis subagent smoke:
- tool_search for gbrain_readonly returned 0 tools
- ALL_TOOLS had no gbrain/brain/readonly match
- stats/search/query/get_page checks could not run because the tool was absent
```

The gateway policy log for that same fresh Dennis spawn shows the exact failure mode:

```text
agents/tool-policy removed 17 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding): ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via agents.dennis-ritchie.tools.deny: web_fetch
agents/tool-policy removed 7 tool(s) via subagent tools.deny: ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via inherited tools: gbrain_readonly
```

The deployment config already grants Dennis and Albert `tools.alsoAllow` for `gbrain_readonly`, so this is not a missing config grant or plugin-load issue. The runtime is stripping the target-agent allowed tool from the child session through the inherited allowlist.

## Proof Boundary

Post-fix production proof requires this source fix to be merged/deployed and the protected gateway/runtime refresh to run. Until then, the only honest live proof available is the failure trace above plus the regression proving the fixed child-session envelope retains the target agent's configured allowlist.

## Scope

This PR is source-only. It does not deploy, change config, restart the gateway, or grant write/admin GBrain access.
